title: Dancing: quadrille and waltz
summary: An interviewer recalls dancing the quadrille and waltz at the Hopes Hall and the talk drifts into discipline; the block ends in ASR repetition.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: And when they be playing them things, I said, Lord, where I was? And yeah, I am 66 years old. And you know, I've been a dancer all my days and I never forgot them steps. Oh, is that right? That's right. Walls and everything else, I never forget that step. Did you do much of the quadrille? Did you ever dance? That's just the most important. I could do them things. We'd like to get you to explain that to us someday on the face. But they don't have quadrille like they used to have a long time ago. Where did you go to dance? And all that. Right here in the same town here. The colony, the Hopes Hall. Oh, yes. In front of me, that's next to the almost white people, you know, in yellow. Yes.
That's a church now, I guess. Yeah.
And child quadrille just give me one of them good dancers. I used to win more prizes in dancing, waltz.

Waltz was a beautiful dance. Two steps and all these kind of things. But you don't find that now. You find them people that scrubbing the floor, breaking your back and your neck. They don't dance like that now. They ain't throwing you that way.

No, I don't like all that. I be looking at them teenagers. I say, in my time, I would mother be hanging around with straps. And great big straps, big as wide as my hand and cut them. Make, you know, taste like your fingers. And then take that and put that on a piece of wood. And I'm telling you, when they get through with you, you say, your legs and everything, you stay, you can't run. You better stay there. You know, I'm waiting. I want to build this bamboo
